title: NRP — Neonatal Resuscitation
sources: Critical Vector — Neonatology Pocket Guide: NRP Algorithm (ABCD)
AHA/AAP Neonatal Resuscitation Program, 8th ed (2021) / ILCOR 2020 (Wyckoff MH et al. Circulation 2020;142:S185-S221)

changelog.change: Initial entry — the NRP 2021 delivery-room sequence: the three questions, initial steps, the HR-triggered escalation (PPV → compressions → epinephrine), doses, and the failure-to-respond checklist.

purpose: The delivery-room resuscitation sequence. Heart rate is the single best indicator of response — reassess it after every intervention. Acrocyanosis alone is a normal transitional finding, not a trigger.
ageRange: Newborn (delivery room; out-of-hospital up to 24 h of life)

body.text: Term gestation? Good tone? Breathing or crying? — YES to all → routine care (warm, dry, skin-to-skin, ongoing evaluation on mother). NO to any → begin warming / drying / stimulation and proceed down the algorithm.

items: Radiant warmer (after cord management per the delayed-cord-clamping protocol). Preterm < 32 wk: plastic wrap / bag, hat, thermal mattress — target axillary 36.5–37.5 °C.
Position supine, neck neutral / slightly extended (shoulder roll if needed).
Suction ONLY if the airway is obstructed or PPV is needed — routine suctioning is no longer recommended, even with meconium.
Dry and stimulate (rub the back, flick the soles); remove wet linen.
Pulse oximeter on the RIGHT hand/wrist (pre-ductal); ECG leads for the most reliable HR.

rows: Apnoeic / gasping, OR HR < 100
Positive-pressure ventilation (PPV) 40–60 breaths/min, starting at 21% O2 for ≥ 35 wk (21–30% for < 35 wk). The rise in HR is the primary measure of effective PPV.
HR not rising / chest not moving after PPV
MR SOPA corrective steps: Mask readjust · Reposition airway · Suction mouth then nose · Open mouth · increase Pressure · Alternative airway (ETT or LMA).
HR < 60 despite ≥ 30 s of effective PPV (chest moving, preferably via an advanced airway)

Start chest compressions + increase FiO2 to 100%. Two-thumb encircling technique. Ratio 3:1 (90 compressions + 30 breaths = 120 events/min). Depth ~1/3 of the AP chest diameter. Reassess HR every 60 s.
HR < 60 despite 60 s of coordinated compressions + PPV
Epinephrine (see below) + a volume expander if blood loss / hypovolaemia is suspected. Give epinephrine while continuing compressions and ventilation.
Epinephrine (1:10,000 = 0.1 mg/mL)
0.01–0.03 mg/kg IV / UVC (preferred). If no IV access yet: 0.05–0.1 mg/kg via ETT
Repeat q3–5 min if HR remains < 60. Prefer the IV/UVC route as soon as it's available.
Volume expander
10 mL/kg NS or O-negative PRBC IV over 5–10 min
For suspected blood loss / hypovolaemia with a poor response to resuscitation. Can repeat.
Dextrose 10%
2 mL/kg IV if hypoglycaemic post-resuscitation
Check glucose once stabilised — especially IDM / preterm / SGA.

body.text: If there's no improvement despite adequate ventilation AND compressions, actively look for: hypovolaemia, pneumothorax, a congenital anomaly (e.g. diaphragmatic hernia — do not bag-mask, intubate + place an OG tube), and correctable technical problems (mask seal, tube position/patency, equipment) BEFORE escalating drug doses. Acrocyanosis with a pink trunk is normal.

buildNote: Tier 1. HR thresholds (100 / 60) are standard NRP and were filled in where the source extraction dropped them. Equipment checklist and the New Ballard Score are separate additions. An APGAR calculator is a natural companion (additive, 0–10).
